Low French-inspired bowl that puzzles most British visitors

The smallest room's centrepiece, plumbed and porcelain
Yellow rubber first mate on every bathtime voyage
Cockerel hammered out of sheet metal, set on a spire to swing with the gusts
Rich white froth worked up from a humble bar
Youngest of the three writing sisters, who lies in a grave by the sea at Scarborough
Heat ore fiercely until the metal runs free of the rock
Glowing and liquid, as lava is, or as iron tipped from the ladle
Surname of the small plain Lowood girl, and the title word of her 1847 story
Plain glass by the mirror, holding brushes and a drop of water
